column.deck: Blaine and Chris set the stage for friendly conflict with opposite Texas picks – one over, one under – as the season begins.
paragraphs: Welcome to the preseason, where aspirations are high and every manager believes they've unlocked the secret to gridiron glory. But before we kick off, a tantalizing clash is already brewing: Blaine vs. Chris, head-to-head over Texas. Each manager has staked a claim on the Longhorns' 9.5 win line, but in opposite directions. Blaine, with a flair for the contrarian, has taken the under. It’s a pick spiked with a dash of personal history, given his Longhorn-in-law situation — a familial quirk that never fails to amuse. Blaine is counting on a challenging SEC schedule, which boasts eight top-25 opponents, to keep Texas under the line.

Chris, meanwhile, is on the other side of the fence, banking on Texas to clear 9.5 wins. Known for his measured approach, Chris likely sees potential for upset wins that the numbers aren’t accounting for, despite the implied expectation of 7.819 wins. The projection gives him just a 14% chance of being right, but Chris isn’t one to be easily daunted. His pick is a testament to optimism, perhaps influenced by his time in Paris — a place that taught him a thing or two about bold moves. As the games unfold, this friendly duel promises to be a subplot worth watching.

Now, Jonathan, let’s talk about Oregon. You’ve taken the Ducks over 10.5 wins, but the numbers aren’t on your side. SP+ sees them finishing with just 9.456 wins. That’s a disagreement of 1.044 games — a sizable gap for any manager to navigate. It’s a bold move for a man known for his rigorous approach, and one that could either showcase your knack for finding hidden value or prove to be as elusive as a reliable wide receiver. We’ll watch this one closely, hoping the calculations align more with liftoff than a crash landing.
That's the column. Don't take the points personally. They were always going to be exactly what they are.
